sections.content: How many people stayed in Chinnor after gaining qualifications?

Chinnor is a small town in the South East. Chinnor does not have its own university.

Chinnor has lower levels of deprivation.

Overall, Chinnor ended up with:

  • fewer graduates than it produced
Note: all towns and cities in this analysis are defined based on population size only. This means that some cities are classed as towns because of their population.

Let's explore this further

There were 250 state-school pupils from Chinnor who sat their GCSEs between the 2007 to 2008 and the 2010 to 2011 school years.

Of these, 90 (36%) went on to gain degree-level qualifications (level 6+ as defined by The Office of Qualifications and Examinations Regulation, or Ofqual ). We will call these people graduates.

Another 90 (36%) went on to gain other advanced post-16 qualifications, such as A-Levels, a foundation degree or higher apprenticeship (levels 3-5 as defined by Ofqual). In this tool, we will refer to these non-graduates with advanced qualifications as “qualified non-graduates", for brevity.

The charts below compare Chinnor to other English towns and cities using three measures:

  • what proportion of Chinnor's pupils became graduates or qualified non-graduates by the 2017 to 2018 academic year
  • of those graduates and qualified non-graduates, the percentages that lived in Chinnor in the 2018 to 2019 academic year
  • how many graduates and qualified non-graduates from elsewhere came to live there by 2018 to 2019, relative to the number who sat their GCSEs there

In some towns, some of this information may not be available because of small sample sizes.
The size and deprivation level of a town, as well as the qualification levels of older residents, were all related to students' educational attainment. Read our previous analysis.

Of those in Chinnor's GCSE cohort:

  • 25 graduates left the South East

In 2018 to 2019, 36% of graduates living in Chinnor had moved there from elsewhere

In the 2018 to 2019 academic year, there were 70 graduates from our cohort living in Chinnor, compared with the 90 graduates who had lived there when they sat their GCSEs.

In the 2018 to 2019 academic year, 57% of graduates had sat their GCSEs in Chinnor, while 36% had moved there from elsewhere.
